// swiftlint:disable all
import Foundation

// Depending on the consumer's build setup, the low-level FFI code
// might be in a separate module, or it might be compiled inline into
// this module. This is a bit of light hackery to work with both.
#if canImport(FirstcutCoreFFI)
import FirstcutCoreFFI
#endif

fileprivate extension RustBuffer {
    // Allocate a new buffer, copying the contents of a `UInt8` array.
    init(bytes: [UInt8]) {
        let rbuf = bytes.withUnsafeBufferPointer { ptr in
            RustBuffer.from(ptr)
        }
        self.init(capacity: rbuf.capacity, len: rbuf.len, data: rbuf.data)
    }

    static func empty() -> RustBuffer {
        RustBuffer(capacity: 0, len:0, data: nil)
    }

    static func from(_ ptr: UnsafeBufferPointer<UInt8>) -> RustBuffer {
        try! rustCall { ffi_firstcut_core_rustbuffer_from_bytes(ForeignBytes(bufferPointer: ptr), $0) }
    }

    // Frees the buffer in place.
    // The buffer must not be used after this is called.
    func deallocate() {
        try! rustCall { ffi_firstcut_core_rustbuffer_free(self, $0) }
    }
}

fileprivate extension ForeignBytes {
    init(bufferPointer: UnsafeBufferPointer<UInt8>) {
        self.init(len: Int32(bufferPointer.count), data: bufferPointer.baseAddress)
    }

    init(rawBufferPointer: UnsafeRawBufferPointer) {
        self.init(
            len: Int32(rawBufferPointer.count),
            data: rawBufferPointer.baseAddress?.assumingMemoryBound(to: UInt8.self)
        )
    }
}

// Converter for `&[u8]` / `[ByRef] bytes` arguments.
//
// Conforms to `FfiConverter` so the compiler enforces the full converter
// method set. Only the scope-bound `lower(_:_body:)` overload is sound —
// zero-copy byte buffers only flow foreign -> Rust, and only in argument
// position. The four protocol-witness methods (`lift`, `lower`, `read`,
// `write`) `fatalError` at runtime if anyone reaches them.
//
// The scope-bound `lower` takes a closure because the `ForeignBytes`
// pointer is only guaranteed valid for the duration of
// `Data.withUnsafeBytes`. Callers must run the full FFI call inside
// the closure body.
fileprivate enum FfiConverterByRefBytes: FfiConverter {
    typealias SwiftType = Data
    typealias FfiType = ForeignBytes

    static func lower<R>(_ value: Data, _ body: (ForeignBytes) throws -> R) rethrows -> R {
        return try value.withUnsafeBytes { rawBuf in
            try body(ForeignBytes(rawBufferPointer: rawBuf))
        }
    }

    static func lower(_ value: Data) -> ForeignBytes {
        fatalError("ByRef bytes cannot use the plain lower: returning ForeignBytes escapes the Data.withUnsafeBytes scope. Use the scope-bound lower(_:_body:) overload instead.")
    }

    static func lift(_ value: ForeignBytes) throws -> Data {
        fatalError("ByRef bytes cannot be lifted: zero-copy &[u8] only flows foreign->Rust")
    }

    static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> Data {
        fatalError("ByRef bytes cannot be read from a buffer: zero-copy &[u8] is only supported in argument position, not nested in records/options/etc.")
    }

    static func write(_ value: Data, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        fatalError("ByRef bytes cannot be written to a buffer: zero-copy &[u8] is only supported in argument position, not nested in records/options/etc.")
    }
}

// For every type used in the interface, we provide helper methods for conveniently
// lifting and lowering that type from C-compatible data, and for reading and writing
// values of that type in a buffer.

// Helper classes/extensions that don't change.
// Someday, this will be in a library of its own.

fileprivate extension Data {
    init(rustBuffer: RustBuffer) {
        self.init(
            bytesNoCopy: rustBuffer.data!,
            count: Int(rustBuffer.len),
            deallocator: .none
        )
    }
}

// Define reader functionality.  Normally this would be defined in a class or
// struct, but we use standalone functions instead in order to make external
// types work.
//
// With external types, one swift source file needs to be able to call the read
// method on another source file's FfiConverter, but then what visibility
// should Reader have?
// - If Reader is fileprivate, then this means the read() must also
//   be fileprivate, which doesn't work with external types.
// - If Reader is internal/public, we'll get compile errors since both source
//   files will try define the same type.
//
// Instead, the read() method and these helper functions input a tuple of data

fileprivate func createReader(data: Data) -> (data: Data, offset: Data.Index) {
    (data: data, offset: 0)
}

// Reads an integer at the current offset, in big-endian order, and advances
// the offset on success. Throws if reading the integer would move the
// offset past the end of the buffer.
fileprivate func readInt<T: FixedWidthInteger>(_ reader: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> T {
    let range = reader.offset..<reader.offset + MemoryLayout<T>.size
    guard reader.data.count >= range.upperBound else {
        throw UniffiInternalError.bufferOverflow
    }
    if T.self == UInt8.self {
        let value = reader.data[reader.offset]
        reader.offset += 1
        return value as! T
    }
    var value: T = 0
    let _ = withUnsafeMutableBytes(of: &value, { reader.data.copyBytes(to: $0, from: range)})
    reader.offset = range.upperBound
    return value.bigEndian
}

// Reads an arbitrary number of bytes, to be used to read
// raw bytes, this is useful when lifting strings
fileprivate func readBytes(_ reader: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index), count: Int) throws -> Array<UInt8> {
    let range = reader.offset..<(reader.offset+count)
    guard reader.data.count >= range.upperBound else {
        throw UniffiInternalError.bufferOverflow
    }
    var value = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: count)
    value.withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer({ buffer in
        reader.data.copyBytes(to: buffer, from: range)
    })
    reader.offset = range.upperBound
    return value
}

// Reads a float at the current offset.
fileprivate func readFloat(_ reader: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> Float {
    return Float(bitPattern: try readInt(&reader))
}

// Reads a float at the current offset.
fileprivate func readDouble(_ reader: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> Double {
    return Double(bitPattern: try readInt(&reader))
}

// Indicates if the offset has reached the end of the buffer.
fileprivate func hasRemaining(_ reader: (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) -> Bool {
    return reader.offset < reader.data.count
}

// Define writer functionality.  Normally this would be defined in a class or
// struct, but we use standalone functions instead in order to make external
// types work.  See the above discussion on Readers for details.

fileprivate func createWriter() -> [UInt8] {
    return []
}

fileprivate func writeBytes<S>(_ writer: inout [UInt8], _ byteArr: S) where S: Sequence, S.Element == UInt8 {
    writer.append(contentsOf: byteArr)
}

// Writes an integer in big-endian order.
//
// Warning: make sure what you are trying to write
// is in the correct type!
fileprivate func writeInt<T: FixedWidthInteger>(_ writer: inout [UInt8], _ value: T) {
    var value = value.bigEndian
    withUnsafeBytes(of: &value) { writer.append(contentsOf: $0) }
}

fileprivate func writeFloat(_ writer: inout [UInt8], _ value: Float) {
    writeInt(&writer, value.bitPattern)
}

fileprivate func writeDouble(_ writer: inout [UInt8], _ value: Double) {
    writeInt(&writer, value.bitPattern)
}

// Protocol for types that transfer other types across the FFI. This is
// analogous to the Rust trait of the same name.
fileprivate protocol FfiConverter {
    associatedtype FfiType
    associatedtype SwiftType

    static func lift(_ value: FfiType) throws -> SwiftType
    static func lower(_ value: SwiftType) -> FfiType
    static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> SwiftType
    static func write(_ value: SwiftType, into buf: inout [UInt8])
}

// Types conforming to `Primitive` pass themselves directly over the FFI.
fileprivate protocol FfiConverterPrimitive: FfiConverter where FfiType == SwiftType { }

extension FfiConverterPrimitive {
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public static func lift(_ value: FfiType) throws -> SwiftType {
        return value
    }

#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public static func lower(_ value: SwiftType) -> FfiType {
        return value
    }
}

// Types conforming to `FfiConverterRustBuffer` lift and lower into a `RustBuffer`.
// Used for complex types where it's hard to write a custom lift/lower.
fileprivate protocol FfiConverterRustBuffer: FfiConverter where FfiType == RustBuffer {}

extension FfiConverterRustBuffer {
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public static func lift(_ buf: RustBuffer) throws -> SwiftType {
        var reader = createReader(data: Data(rustBuffer: buf))
        let value = try read(from: &reader)
        if hasRemaining(reader) {
            throw UniffiInternalError.incompleteData
        }
        buf.deallocate()
        return value
    }

#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public static func lower(_ value: SwiftType) -> RustBuffer {
          var writer = createWriter()
          write(value, into: &writer)
          return RustBuffer(bytes: writer)
    }
}
// An error type for FFI errors. These errors occur at the UniFFI level, not
// the library level.
fileprivate enum UniffiInternalError: LocalizedError {
    case bufferOverflow
    case incompleteData
    case unexpectedOptionalTag
    case unexpectedEnumCase
    case unexpectedNullPointer
    case unexpectedRustCallStatusCode
    case unexpectedRustCallError
    case unexpectedStaleHandle
    case rustPanic(_ message: String)

    public var errorDescription: String? {
        switch self {
        case .bufferOverflow: return "Reading the requested value would read past the end of the buffer"
        case .incompleteData: return "The buffer still has data after lifting its containing value"
        case .unexpectedOptionalTag: return "Unexpected optional tag; should be 0 or 1"
        case .unexpectedEnumCase: return "Raw enum value doesn't match any cases"
        case .unexpectedNullPointer: return "Raw pointer value was null"
        case .unexpectedRustCallStatusCode: return "Unexpected RustCallStatus code"
        case .unexpectedRustCallError: return "CALL_ERROR but no errorClass specified"
        case .unexpectedStaleHandle: return "The object in the handle map has been dropped already"
        case let .rustPanic(message): return message
        }
    }
}

fileprivate extension NSLock {
    func withLock<T>(f: () throws -> T) rethrows -> T {
        self.lock()
        defer { self.unlock() }
        return try f()
    }
}

fileprivate let CALL_SUCCESS: Int8 = 0
fileprivate let CALL_ERROR: Int8 = 1
fileprivate let CALL_UNEXPECTED_ERROR: Int8 = 2
fileprivate let CALL_CANCELLED: Int8 = 3

fileprivate extension RustCallStatus {
    init() {
        self.init(
            code: CALL_SUCCESS,
            errorBuf: RustBuffer.init(
                capacity: 0,
                len: 0,
                data: nil
            )
        )
    }
}

private func rustCall<T>(_ callback: (UnsafeMutablePointer<RustCallStatus>) -> T) throws -> T {
    let neverThrow: ((RustBuffer) throws -> Never)? = nil
    return try makeRustCall(callback, errorHandler: neverThrow)
}

private func rustCallWithError<T, E: Swift.Error>(
    _ errorHandler: @escaping (RustBuffer) throws -> E,
    _ callback: (UnsafeMutablePointer<RustCallStatus>) -> T) throws -> T {
    try makeRustCall(callback, errorHandler: errorHandler)
}

private func makeRustCall<T, E: Swift.Error>(
    _ callback: (UnsafeMutablePointer<RustCallStatus>) -> T,
    errorHandler: ((RustBuffer) throws -> E)?
) throws -> T {
    uniffiEnsureFirstcutCoreInitialized()
    var callStatus = RustCallStatus.init()
    let returnedVal = callback(&callStatus)
    try uniffiCheckCallStatus(callStatus: callStatus, errorHandler: errorHandler)
    return returnedVal
}

private func uniffiCheckCallStatus<E: Swift.Error>(
    callStatus: RustCallStatus,
    errorHandler: ((RustBuffer) throws -> E)?
) throws {
    switch callStatus.code {
        case CALL_SUCCESS:
            return

        case CALL_ERROR:
            if let errorHandler = errorHandler {
                throw try errorHandler(callStatus.errorBuf)
            } else {
                callStatus.errorBuf.deallocate()
                throw UniffiInternalError.unexpectedRustCallError
            }

        case CALL_UNEXPECTED_ERROR:
            // When the rust code sees a panic, it tries to construct a RustBuffer
            // with the message.  But if that code panics, then it just sends back
            // an empty buffer.
            if callStatus.errorBuf.len > 0 {
                throw UniffiInternalError.rustPanic(try FfiConverterString.lift(callStatus.errorBuf))
            } else {
                callStatus.errorBuf.deallocate()
                throw UniffiInternalError.rustPanic("Rust panic")
            }

        case CALL_CANCELLED:
            fatalError("Cancellation not supported yet")

        default:
            throw UniffiInternalError.unexpectedRustCallStatusCode
    }
}

private func uniffiTraitInterfaceCall<T>(
    callStatus: UnsafeMutablePointer<RustCallStatus>,
    makeCall: () throws -> T,
    writeReturn: (T) -> ()
) {
    do {
        try writeReturn(makeCall())
    } catch let error {
        callStatus.pointee.code = CALL_UNEXPECTED_ERROR
        callStatus.pointee.errorBuf = FfiConverterString.lower(String(describing: error))
    }
}

private func uniffiTraitInterfaceCallWithError<T, E>(
    callStatus: UnsafeMutablePointer<RustCallStatus>,
    makeCall: () throws -> T,
    writeReturn: (T) -> (),
    lowerError: (E) -> RustBuffer
) {
    do {
        try writeReturn(makeCall())
    } catch let error as E {
        callStatus.pointee.code = CALL_ERROR
        callStatus.pointee.errorBuf = lowerError(error)
    } catch {
        callStatus.pointee.code = CALL_UNEXPECTED_ERROR
        callStatus.pointee.errorBuf = FfiConverterString.lower(String(describing: error))
    }
}
// Initial value and increment amount for handles. 
// These ensure that SWIFT handles always have the lowest bit set
fileprivate let UNIFFI_HANDLEMAP_INITIAL: UInt64 = 1
fileprivate let UNIFFI_HANDLEMAP_DELTA: UInt64 = 2

fileprivate final class UniffiHandleMap<T>: @unchecked Sendable {
    // All mutation happens with this lock held, which is why we implement @unchecked Sendable.
    private let lock = NSLock()
    private var map: [UInt64: T] = [:]
    private var currentHandle: UInt64 = UNIFFI_HANDLEMAP_INITIAL

    func insert(obj: T) -> UInt64 {
        lock.withLock {
            return doInsert(obj)
        }
    }

    // Low-level insert function, this assumes `lock` is held.
    private func doInsert(_ obj: T) -> UInt64 {
        let handle = currentHandle
        currentHandle += UNIFFI_HANDLEMAP_DELTA
        map[handle] = obj
        return handle
    }

     func get(handle: UInt64) throws -> T {
        try lock.withLock {
            guard let obj = map[handle] else {
                throw UniffiInternalError.unexpectedStaleHandle
            }
            return obj
        }
    }

     func clone(handle: UInt64) throws -> UInt64 {
        try lock.withLock {
            guard let obj = map[handle] else {
                throw UniffiInternalError.unexpectedStaleHandle
            }
            return doInsert(obj)
        }
    }

    @discardableResult
    func remove(handle: UInt64) throws -> T {
        try lock.withLock {
            guard let obj = map.removeValue(forKey: handle) else {
                throw UniffiInternalError.unexpectedStaleHandle
            }
            return obj
        }
    }

    var count: Int {
        get {
            map.count
        }
    }
}

#endif
fileprivate struct FfiConverterBool : FfiConverter {
    typealias FfiType = Int8
    typealias SwiftType = Bool

    public static func lift(_ value: Int8) throws -> Bool {
        return value != 0
    }

    public static func lower(_ value: Bool) -> Int8 {
        return value ? 1 : 0
    }

    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> Bool {
        return try lift(readInt(&buf))
    }

    public static func write(_ value: Bool, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        writeInt(&buf, lower(value))
    }
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
fileprivate struct FfiConverterString: FfiConverter {
    typealias SwiftType = String
    typealias FfiType = RustBuffer

    public static func lift(_ value: RustBuffer) throws -> String {
        defer {
            value.deallocate()
        }
        if value.data == nil {
            return String()
        }
        let bytes = UnsafeBufferPointer<UInt8>(start: value.data!, count: Int(value.len))
        // Use Swift's native UTF-8 decoder; `String(bytes:encoding:.utf8)` goes
        // through Foundation's NSString and silently strips a leading U+FEFF BOM.
        // Invalid UTF-8 substitutes U+FFFD instead of trapping (unreachable
        // given Rust's `String` invariant).
        return String(decoding: bytes, as: UTF8.self)
    }

    public static func lower(_ value: String) -> RustBuffer {
        return value.utf8CString.withUnsafeBufferPointer { ptr in
            // The swift string gives us int8_t, we want uint8_t.
            ptr.withMemoryRebound(to: UInt8.self) { ptr in
                // The swift string gives us a trailing null byte, we don't want it.
                let buf = UnsafeBufferPointer(rebasing: ptr.prefix(upTo: ptr.count - 1))
                return RustBuffer.from(buf)
            }
        }
    }

    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> String {
        let len: Int32 = try readInt(&buf)
        // See `lift` above for why we avoid Foundation's NSString-backed decoder here.
        return String(decoding: try readBytes(&buf, count: Int(len)), as: UTF8.self)
    }

    public static func write(_ value: String, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        let len = Int32(value.utf8.count)
        writeInt(&buf, len)
        writeBytes(&buf, value.utf8)
    }
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
fileprivate struct FfiConverterData: FfiConverterRustBuffer {
    typealias SwiftType = Data

    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> Data {
        let len: Int32 = try readInt(&buf)
        return Data(try readBytes(&buf, count: Int(len)))
    }

    public static func write(_ value: Data, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        let len = Int32(value.count)
        writeInt(&buf, len)
        writeBytes(&buf, value)
    }
}




/**
 * The session's callbacks, as a Swift protocol the app conforms to.
 *
 * A UniFFI callback interface, so `app-logic` gets `SessionListener` pushed from the core instead
 * of polling. Every method is called on a core thread, never the main thread — hop to the main
 * actor before touching UI state.
 */
public protocol FfiSessionListener: AnyObject, Sendable {
    
    /**
     * Only unvisited batches can differ: a batch the user has been in is frozen (todo.md §5.4).
     */
    func onBatchesChanged(batches: [FfiBatch]) 
    
    /**
     * FSEvents: files were added to or removed from the folder.
     */
    func onFilesChanged() 
    
    /**
     * A sidecar could not be written. The database is still correct; only the copy in the folder
     * is behind.
     */
    func onXmpError(photo: UInt64, message: String) 
    
    /**
     * The folder moved or was renamed since the last time this shoot was opened.
     */
    func onSessionMoved(from: String) 
    
}
/**
 * The session's callbacks, as a Swift protocol the app conforms to.
 *
 * A UniFFI callback interface, so `app-logic` gets `SessionListener` pushed from the core instead
 * of polling. Every method is called on a core thread, never the main thread — hop to the main
 * actor before touching UI state.
 */
open class FfiSessionListenerImpl: FfiSessionListener, @unchecked Sendable {
    fileprivate let handle: UInt64

    /// Used to instantiate a [FFIObject] without an actual handle, for fakes in tests, mostly.
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public struct NoHandle {
        public init() {}
    }

    // TODO: We'd like this to be `private` but for Swifty reasons,
    // we can't implement `FfiConverter` without making this `required` and we can't
    // make it `required` without making it `public`.
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    required public init(unsafeFromHandle handle: UInt64) {
        self.handle = handle
    }

    // This constructor can be used to instantiate a fake object.
    // - Parameter noHandle: Placeholder value so we can have a constructor separate from the default empty one that may be implemented for classes extending [FFIObject].
    //
    // - Warning:
    //     Any object instantiated with this constructor cannot be passed to an actual Rust-backed object. Since there isn't a backing handle the FFI lower functions will crash.
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public init(noHandle: NoHandle) {
        self.handle = 0
    }

#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public func uniffiCloneHandle() -> UInt64 {
        return try! rustCall { uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_clone_ffisessionlistener(self.handle, $0) }
    }
    // No primary constructor declared for this class.

    deinit {
        if handle == 0 {
            // Mock objects have handle=0 don't try to free them
            return
        }

        try! rustCall { uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_free_ffisessionlistener(handle, $0) }
    }

    

    
    /**
     * Only unvisited batches can differ: a batch the user has been in is frozen (todo.md §5.4).
     */
open func onBatchesChanged(batches: [FfiBatch])  {try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_ffisessionlistener_on_batches_changed(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiBatch.lower(batches),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * FSEvents: files were added to or removed from the folder.
     */
open func onFilesChanged()  {try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_ffisessionlistener_on_files_changed(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * A sidecar could not be written. The database is still correct; only the copy in the folder
     * is behind.
     */
open func onXmpError(photo: UInt64, message: String)  {try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_ffisessionlistener_on_xmp_error(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterUInt64.lower(photo),
        FfiConverterString.lower(message),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * The folder moved or was renamed since the last time this shoot was opened.
     */
open func onSessionMoved(from: String)  {try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_ffisessionlistener_on_session_moved(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterString.lower(from),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    

    
}



// Put the implementation in a struct so we don't pollute the top-level namespace
fileprivate struct UniffiCallbackInterfaceFfiSessionListener {

    // Create the VTable using a series of closures.
    // Swift automatically converts these into C callback functions.
    //
    // Store the vtable directly.
    static let vtable: UniffiVTableCallbackInterfaceFfiSessionListener = UniffiVTableCallbackInterfaceFfiSessionListener(
        uniffiFree: { (uniffiHandle: UInt64) -> () in
            do {
                try FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener.handleMap.remove(handle: uniffiHandle)
            } catch {
                print("Uniffi callback interface FfiSessionListener: handle missing in uniffiFree")
            }
        },
        uniffiClone: { (uniffiHandle: UInt64) -> UInt64 in
            do {
                return try FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener.handleMap.clone(handle: uniffiHandle)
            } catch {
                fatalError("Uniffi callback interface FfiSessionListener: handle missing in uniffiClone")
            }
        },
        onBatchesChanged: { (
            uniffiHandle: UInt64,
            batches: RustBuffer,
            uniffiOutReturn: UnsafeMutableRawPointer,
            uniffiCallStatus: UnsafeMutablePointer<RustCallStatus>
        ) in
            let makeCall = {
                () throws -> () in
                guard let uniffiObj = try? FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener.handleMap.get(handle: uniffiHandle) else {
                    throw UniffiInternalError.unexpectedStaleHandle
                }
                return uniffiObj.onBatchesChanged(
                     batches: try FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiBatch.lift(batches)
                )
            }

            
            let writeReturn = { () }
            uniffiTraitInterfaceCall(
                callStatus: uniffiCallStatus,
                makeCall: makeCall,
                writeReturn: writeReturn
            )
        },
        onFilesChanged: { (
            uniffiHandle: UInt64,
            uniffiOutReturn: UnsafeMutableRawPointer,
            uniffiCallStatus: UnsafeMutablePointer<RustCallStatus>
        ) in
            let makeCall = {
                () throws -> () in
                guard let uniffiObj = try? FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener.handleMap.get(handle: uniffiHandle) else {
                    throw UniffiInternalError.unexpectedStaleHandle
                }
                return uniffiObj.onFilesChanged(
                )
            }

            
            let writeReturn = { () }
            uniffiTraitInterfaceCall(
                callStatus: uniffiCallStatus,
                makeCall: makeCall,
                writeReturn: writeReturn
            )
        },
        onXmpError: { (
            uniffiHandle: UInt64,
            photo: UInt64,
            message: RustBuffer,
            uniffiOutReturn: UnsafeMutableRawPointer,
            uniffiCallStatus: UnsafeMutablePointer<RustCallStatus>
        ) in
            let makeCall = {
                () throws -> () in
                guard let uniffiObj = try? FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener.handleMap.get(handle: uniffiHandle) else {
                    throw UniffiInternalError.unexpectedStaleHandle
                }
                return uniffiObj.onXmpError(
                     photo: try FfiConverterUInt64.lift(photo),
                     message: try FfiConverterString.lift(message)
                )
            }

            
            let writeReturn = { () }
            uniffiTraitInterfaceCall(
                callStatus: uniffiCallStatus,
                makeCall: makeCall,
                writeReturn: writeReturn
            )
        },
        onSessionMoved: { (
            uniffiHandle: UInt64,
            from: RustBuffer,
            uniffiOutReturn: UnsafeMutableRawPointer,
            uniffiCallStatus: UnsafeMutablePointer<RustCallStatus>
        ) in
            let makeCall = {
                () throws -> () in
                guard let uniffiObj = try? FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener.handleMap.get(handle: uniffiHandle) else {
                    throw UniffiInternalError.unexpectedStaleHandle
                }
                return uniffiObj.onSessionMoved(
                     from: try FfiConverterString.lift(from)
                )
            }

            
            let writeReturn = { () }
            uniffiTraitInterfaceCall(
                callStatus: uniffiCallStatus,
                makeCall: makeCall,
                writeReturn: writeReturn
            )
        }
    )

    // Rust stores this pointer for future callback invocations, so it must live
    // for the process lifetime (not just for the init function call).
    //
    // `nonisolated(unsafe)` is needed under Swift 6 strict concurrency.
    // This is safe because the pointee is initialized once during static init
    // and never mutated by either side of the FFI.  Its fields are C function pointers.
    nonisolated(unsafe) static let vtablePtr: UnsafePointer<UniffiVTableCallbackInterfaceFfiSessionListener> = {
        let ptr = UnsafeMutablePointer<UniffiVTableCallbackInterfaceFfiSessionListener>.allocate(capacity: 1)
        ptr.initialize(to: vtable)
        return UnsafePointer(ptr)
    }()
}

private func uniffiCallbackInitFfiSessionListener() {
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_init_callback_vtable_ffisessionlistener(UniffiCallbackInterfaceFfiSessionListener.vtablePtr)
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public struct FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener: FfiConverter {
    fileprivate static let handleMap = UniffiHandleMap<FfiSessionListener>()

    typealias FfiType = UInt64
    typealias SwiftType = FfiSessionListener

    public static func lift(_ handle: UInt64) throws -> FfiSessionListener {
        if ((handle & 1) == 0) {
            // Rust-generated handle, construct a new class that uses the handle to implement the
            // interface
            return FfiSessionListenerImpl(unsafeFromHandle: handle)
        } else {
            // Swift-generated handle, get the object from the handle map
            return try handleMap.remove(handle: handle)
        }
    }

    public static func lower(_ value: FfiSessionListener) -> UInt64 {
         if let rustImpl = value as? FfiSessionListenerImpl {
             // Rust-implemented object.  Clone the handle and return it
            return rustImpl.uniffiCloneHandle()
         } else {
            // Swift object, generate a new vtable handle and return that.
            return handleMap.insert(obj: value)
         }
    }

    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> FfiSessionListener {
        let handle: UInt64 = try readInt(&buf)
        return try lift(handle)
    }

    public static func write(_ value: FfiSessionListener, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        writeInt(&buf, lower(value))
    }
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener_lift(_ handle: UInt64) throws -> FfiSessionListener {
    return try FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener.lift(handle)
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener_lower(_ value: FfiSessionListener) -> UInt64 {
    return FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener.lower(value)
}






/**
 * A listener that discards every callback, for the app stages that do not care yet.
 *
 * Swift: `NullListener()`.
 */
public protocol NullListenerProtocol: AnyObject, Sendable {
    
}
/**
 * A listener that discards every callback, for the app stages that do not care yet.
 *
 * Swift: `NullListener()`.
 */
open class NullListener: NullListenerProtocol, @unchecked Sendable {
    fileprivate let handle: UInt64

    /// Used to instantiate a [FFIObject] without an actual handle, for fakes in tests, mostly.
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public struct NoHandle {
        public init() {}
    }

    // TODO: We'd like this to be `private` but for Swifty reasons,
    // we can't implement `FfiConverter` without making this `required` and we can't
    // make it `required` without making it `public`.
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    required public init(unsafeFromHandle handle: UInt64) {
        self.handle = handle
    }

    // This constructor can be used to instantiate a fake object.
    // - Parameter noHandle: Placeholder value so we can have a constructor separate from the default empty one that may be implemented for classes extending [FFIObject].
    //
    // - Warning:
    //     Any object instantiated with this constructor cannot be passed to an actual Rust-backed object. Since there isn't a backing handle the FFI lower functions will crash.
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public init(noHandle: NoHandle) {
        self.handle = 0
    }

#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public func uniffiCloneHandle() -> UInt64 {
        return try! rustCall { uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_clone_nulllistener(self.handle, $0) }
    }
public convenience init() {
    let handle =
        try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_constructor_nulllistener_new(uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
    self.init(unsafeFromHandle: handle)
}

    deinit {
        if handle == 0 {
            // Mock objects have handle=0 don't try to free them
            return
        }

        try! rustCall { uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_free_nulllistener(handle, $0) }
    }

    

    

    
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public struct FfiConverterTypeNullListener: FfiConverter {
    typealias FfiType = UInt64
    typealias SwiftType = NullListener

    public static func lift(_ handle: UInt64) throws -> NullListener {
        return NullListener(unsafeFromHandle: handle)
    }

    public static func lower(_ value: NullListener) -> UInt64 {
        return value.uniffiCloneHandle()
    }

    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> NullListener {
        let handle: UInt64 = try readInt(&buf)
        return try lift(handle)
    }

    public static func write(_ value: NullListener, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        writeInt(&buf, lower(value))
    }
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeNullListener_lift(_ handle: UInt64) throws -> NullListener {
    return try FfiConverterTypeNullListener.lift(handle)
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeNullListener_lower(_ value: NullListener) -> UInt64 {
    return FfiConverterTypeNullListener.lower(value)
}






/**
 * The session handle the app holds: Swift `try Session.open(folder:listener:)`.
 *
 * A UniFFI object, so Swift holds a reference with `Arc` semantics and Rust owns the state. Every
 * method takes `&self` and the core locks internally, so a rating from the UI thread and a sidecar
 * write on the writer thread cannot race.
 */
public protocol SessionProtocol: AnyObject, Sendable {
    
    /**
     * How this folder is batched. Saved per folder; Plays until the user picks Bursts.
     */
    func batchingMode()  -> FfiBatchingMode
    
    /**
     * Flushes and stops the writer. The session is unusable afterwards, so the app drops its
     * handle.
     */
    func close() 
    
    /**
     * Does what the plan says, logging every operation so `undo_finish` works even after a
     * relaunch. A destination that has since become occupied fails that one operation instead of
     * overwriting the file that is there.
     */
    func executeFinish(plan: FfiFinishPlan) throws  -> FfiFinishReport
    
    /**
     * Writes every pending sidecar. Called on a batch change and before the app quits.
     *
     * Returns only once the last write has landed on disk, so a quit immediately after this
     * cannot lose a rating the user just made.
     */
    func flush() 
    
    /**
     * The canonical shoot folder.
     */
    func folder()  -> String
    
    /**
     * Marks a batch as seen, which freezes it (todo.md §5.4).
     */
    func markVisited(batch: UInt64) throws 
    
    /**
     * New, the same place, or re-matched after a move. The app shows a note when it is `moved`.
     */
    func matched()  -> FfiMatchKind
    
    /**
     * The dry run: everything Finish would do, in order, without touching a file. Planned with the
     * session's own rating mode, so the preview and the filmstrip agree about what is kept.
     */
    func planFinish(options: FfiFinishOptions) throws  -> FfiFinishPlan
    
    func ratingMode()  -> FfiRatingMode
    
    /**
     * Re-applies the newest undone change, or `nil` when there is nothing to redo.
     */
    func redo()  -> FfiChange?
    
    /**
     * Re-applies one undone step, as `undo_step`.
     */
    func redoStep()  -> [FfiChange]
    
    /**
     * Re-reads the folder, recognising renamed files so a rating survives a rename in Finder
     * (REV-68).
     */
    func rescan() throws  -> FfiScanResult
    
    /**
     * Sets and saves the batching mode, then re-cuts the batches that have not been visited.
     */
    func setBatchingMode(mode: FfiBatchingMode) throws 
    
    /**
     * Records where the user is, so reopening the shoot lands in the same place. Also marks the
     * batch visited, which freezes it against re-batching.
     */
    func setCursor(cursor: FfiCursor) throws 
    
    /**
     * The keep threshold in stars mode (Settings → General): 4 ("4 and 5 stars") or 5 ("only 5
     * stars"); anything else is clamped. Finish and `tier_counts` follow it.
     */
    func setKeepThreshold(stars: UInt8) 
    
    /**
     * Records a rating. Returns in the time one WAL transaction takes; the XMP sidecar is written
     * on a debounced background thread, so the app never waits on a file write.
     */
    func setRating(photo: UInt64, rating: FfiRating) throws  -> FfiChange
    
    /**
     * Switches rating mode. Existing data is mapped, never rewritten or dropped (todo.md §6).
     */
    func setRatingMode(mode: FfiRatingMode) throws 
    
    /**
     * Rates several photos as one change that one undo reverts whole ("Reject whole batch", an
     * opt-in setting). Photos whose rating is already the one asked for are left out of the
     * result and of the undo step.
     */
    func setRatings(ratings: [FfiPhotoRating]) throws  -> [FfiChange]
    
    /**
     * Settings → Metadata: whether ratings are mirrored to `.xmp` sidecars, for which files, and
     * what a Keep is written as. `keep_stars` is 1...=5, or `keep_label` replaces it.
     */
    func setXmpSettings(writeSidecars: Bool, sidecarsForNonRaw: Bool, keepStars: UInt8, keepLabel: FfiColorLabel?) throws 
    
    /**
     * Everything the UI draws from, in one value.
     */
    func snapshot()  -> FfiSessionSnapshot
    
    /**
     * Submits visual signatures from the pipeline, which may re-batch the unvisited batches.
     */
    func submitVisualSigs(sigs: [FfiVisualSigEntry]) 
    
    /**
     * Tier counts for the Finish summary, in the given mode (todo.md §6.1).
     */
    func tierCounts(mode: FfiRatingMode)  -> [FfiTier: UInt32]
    
    /**
     * Reverts the newest change, or `nil` when there is nothing to undo.
     */
    func undo()  -> FfiChange?
    
    /**
     * Reverses the last Finish run. Refused, with the reason, if it included a permanent delete.
     */
    func undoFinish() throws  -> FfiFinishReport
    
    /**
     * Reverts one undo step and reports every photo it put back: one for a single rating, the
     * whole group for a `set_ratings` call. Empty when there is nothing to undo.
     */
    func undoStep()  -> [FfiChange]
    
}
/**
 * The session handle the app holds: Swift `try Session.open(folder:listener:)`.
 *
 * A UniFFI object, so Swift holds a reference with `Arc` semantics and Rust owns the state. Every
 * method takes `&self` and the core locks internally, so a rating from the UI thread and a sidecar
 * write on the writer thread cannot race.
 */
open class Session: SessionProtocol, @unchecked Sendable {
    fileprivate let handle: UInt64

    /// Used to instantiate a [FFIObject] without an actual handle, for fakes in tests, mostly.
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public struct NoHandle {
        public init() {}
    }

    // TODO: We'd like this to be `private` but for Swifty reasons,
    // we can't implement `FfiConverter` without making this `required` and we can't
    // make it `required` without making it `public`.
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    required public init(unsafeFromHandle handle: UInt64) {
        self.handle = handle
    }

    // This constructor can be used to instantiate a fake object.
    // - Parameter noHandle: Placeholder value so we can have a constructor separate from the default empty one that may be implemented for classes extending [FFIObject].
    //
    // - Warning:
    //     Any object instantiated with this constructor cannot be passed to an actual Rust-backed object. Since there isn't a backing handle the FFI lower functions will crash.
#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public init(noHandle: NoHandle) {
        self.handle = 0
    }

#if swift(>=5.8)
    @_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
    public func uniffiCloneHandle() -> UInt64 {
        return try! rustCall { uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_clone_session(self.handle, $0) }
    }
    // No primary constructor declared for this class.

    deinit {
        if handle == 0 {
            // Mock objects have handle=0 don't try to free them
            return
        }

        try! rustCall { uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_free_session(handle, $0) }
    }

    
    /**
     * Scans, orders, provisional-batches and restores the database.
     *
     * The one call that does real work, so the one that can be slow: headers only, and a
     * 1,500-frame Canon shoot is a few seconds on an internal SSD. Pass `NullListener()` when the
     * app has nothing to listen to yet — which is the state while the library grid is still empty
     * and the user has not chosen a folder. UniFFI cannot lift an optional callback interface, so
     * the "no listener" case is an explicit object rather than `nil`.
     */
public static func `open`(folder: String, listener: FfiSessionListener)throws  -> Session  {
    return try  FfiConverterTypeSession_lift(try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_constructor_session_open(
        FfiConverterString.lower(folder),
        FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener_lower(listener),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * [`Session::open`] with the database directory chosen by the caller.
     *
     * The app uses `open`. This exists so a test — or a future portable-sessions build — can keep
     * its databases somewhere other than the user's Application Support folder, instead of writing
     * real session files into the developer's home directory.
     */
public static func openIn(folder: String, sessionsDir: String, listener: FfiSessionListener)throws  -> Session  {
    return try  FfiConverterTypeSession_lift(try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_constructor_session_open_in(
        FfiConverterString.lower(folder),
        FfiConverterString.lower(sessionsDir),
        FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionListener_lower(listener),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    

    
    /**
     * How this folder is batched. Saved per folder; Plays until the user picks Bursts.
     */
open func batchingMode() -> FfiBatchingMode  {
    return try!  FfiConverterTypeFfiBatchingMode_lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_batching_mode(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Flushes and stops the writer. The session is unusable afterwards, so the app drops its
     * handle.
     */
open func close()  {try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_close(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * Does what the plan says, logging every operation so `undo_finish` works even after a
     * relaunch. A destination that has since become occupied fails that one operation instead of
     * overwriting the file that is there.
     */
open func executeFinish(plan: FfiFinishPlan)throws  -> FfiFinishReport  {
    return try  FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishReport_lift(try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_execute_finish(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishPlan_lower(plan),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Writes every pending sidecar. Called on a batch change and before the app quits.
     *
     * Returns only once the last write has landed on disk, so a quit immediately after this
     * cannot lose a rating the user just made.
     */
open func flush()  {try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_flush(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * The canonical shoot folder.
     */
open func folder() -> String  {
    return try!  FfiConverterString.lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_folder(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Marks a batch as seen, which freezes it (todo.md §5.4).
     */
open func markVisited(batch: UInt64)throws   {try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_mark_visited(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterUInt64.lower(batch),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * New, the same place, or re-matched after a move. The app shows a note when it is `moved`.
     */
open func matched() -> FfiMatchKind  {
    return try!  FfiConverterTypeFfiMatchKind_lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_matched(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * The dry run: everything Finish would do, in order, without touching a file. Planned with the
     * session's own rating mode, so the preview and the filmstrip agree about what is kept.
     */
open func planFinish(options: FfiFinishOptions)throws  -> FfiFinishPlan  {
    return try  FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishPlan_lift(try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_plan_finish(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishOptions_lower(options),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
open func ratingMode() -> FfiRatingMode  {
    return try!  FfiConverterTypeFfiRatingMode_lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_rating_mode(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Re-applies the newest undone change, or `nil` when there is nothing to redo.
     */
open func redo() -> FfiChange?  {
    return try!  FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiChange.lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_redo(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Re-applies one undone step, as `undo_step`.
     */
open func redoStep() -> [FfiChange]  {
    return try!  FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiChange.lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_redo_step(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Re-reads the folder, recognising renamed files so a rating survives a rename in Finder
     * (REV-68).
     */
open func rescan()throws  -> FfiScanResult  {
    return try  FfiConverterTypeFfiScanResult_lift(try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_rescan(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Sets and saves the batching mode, then re-cuts the batches that have not been visited.
     */
open func setBatchingMode(mode: FfiBatchingMode)throws   {try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_set_batching_mode(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterTypeFfiBatchingMode_lower(mode),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * Records where the user is, so reopening the shoot lands in the same place. Also marks the
     * batch visited, which freezes it against re-batching.
     */
open func setCursor(cursor: FfiCursor)throws   {try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_set_cursor(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterTypeFfiCursor_lower(cursor),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * The keep threshold in stars mode (Settings → General): 4 ("4 and 5 stars") or 5 ("only 5
     * stars"); anything else is clamped. Finish and `tier_counts` follow it.
     */
open func setKeepThreshold(stars: UInt8)  {try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_set_keep_threshold(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterUInt8.lower(stars),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * Records a rating. Returns in the time one WAL transaction takes; the XMP sidecar is written
     * on a debounced background thread, so the app never waits on a file write.
     */
open func setRating(photo: UInt64, rating: FfiRating)throws  -> FfiChange  {
    return try  FfiConverterTypeFfiChange_lift(try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_set_rating(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterUInt64.lower(photo),
        FfiConverterTypeFfiRating_lower(rating),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Switches rating mode. Existing data is mapped, never rewritten or dropped (todo.md §6).
     */
open func setRatingMode(mode: FfiRatingMode)throws   {try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_set_rating_mode(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterTypeFfiRatingMode_lower(mode),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * Rates several photos as one change that one undo reverts whole ("Reject whole batch", an
     * opt-in setting). Photos whose rating is already the one asked for are left out of the
     * result and of the undo step.
     */
open func setRatings(ratings: [FfiPhotoRating])throws  -> [FfiChange]  {
    return try  FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiChange.lift(try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_set_ratings(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiPhotoRating.lower(ratings),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Settings → Metadata: whether ratings are mirrored to `.xmp` sidecars, for which files, and
     * what a Keep is written as. `keep_stars` is 1...=5, or `keep_label` replaces it.
     */
open func setXmpSettings(writeSidecars: Bool, sidecarsForNonRaw: Bool, keepStars: UInt8, keepLabel: FfiColorLabel?)throws   {try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_set_xmp_settings(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterBool.lower(writeSidecars),
        FfiConverterBool.lower(sidecarsForNonRaw),
        FfiConverterUInt8.lower(keepStars),
        FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiColorLabel.lower(keepLabel),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * Everything the UI draws from, in one value.
     */
open func snapshot() -> FfiSessionSnapshot  {
    return try!  FfiConverterTypeFfiSessionSnapshot_lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_snapshot(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Submits visual signatures from the pipeline, which may re-batch the unvisited batches.
     */
open func submitVisualSigs(sigs: [FfiVisualSigEntry])  {try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_submit_visual_sigs(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiVisualSigEntry.lower(sigs),uniffiCallStatus
    )
}
}
    
    /**
     * Tier counts for the Finish summary, in the given mode (todo.md §6.1).
     */
open func tierCounts(mode: FfiRatingMode) -> [FfiTier: UInt32]  {
    return try!  FfiConverterDictionaryTypeFfiTierUInt32.lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_tier_counts(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),
        FfiConverterTypeFfiRatingMode_lower(mode),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Reverts the newest change, or `nil` when there is nothing to undo.
     */
open func undo() -> FfiChange?  {
    return try!  FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiChange.lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_undo(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Reverses the last Finish run. Refused, with the reason, if it included a permanent delete.
     */
open func undoFinish()throws  -> FfiFinishReport  {
    return try  FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishReport_lift(try rustCallWithError(FfiConverterTypeFfiError_lift) {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_undo_finish(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    
    /**
     * Reverts one undo step and reports every photo it put back: one for a single rating, the
     * whole group for a `set_ratings` call. Empty when there is nothing to undo.
     */
open func undoStep() -> [FfiChange]  {
    return try!  FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiChange.lift(try! rustCall() {
        uniffiCallStatus in
    uniffi_firstcut_core_fn_method_session_undo_step(
            self.uniffiCloneHandle(),uniffiCallStatus
    )
})
}
    

    
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public struct FfiConverterTypeSession: FfiConverter {
    typealias FfiType = UInt64
    typealias SwiftType = Session

    public static func lift(_ handle: UInt64) throws -> Session {
        return Session(unsafeFromHandle: handle)
    }

    public static func lower(_ value: Session) -> UInt64 {
        return value.uniffiCloneHandle()
    }

    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> Session {
        let handle: UInt64 = try readInt(&buf)
        return try lift(handle)
    }

    public static func write(_ value: Session, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        writeInt(&buf, lower(value))
    }
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeSession_lift(_ handle: UInt64) throws -> Session {
    return try FfiConverterTypeSession.lift(handle)
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeSession_lower(_ value: Session) -> UInt64 {
    return FfiConverterTypeSession.lower(value)
}




public struct FfiAfInfo: Equatable, Hashable {
    /**
     * Empty when the camera did not name the mode; the points are still drawn.
     */
    public var areaMode: String
    /**
     * The AF image the coordinates are relative to, so the overlay can letterbox correctly.
     */
    public var imageWidth: UInt32
    public var imageHeight: UInt32
    public var points: [FfiAfPoint]
    /**
     * Indices the camera reports as in focus, in the same units exiftool prints.
     */
    public var pointsInFocus: [UInt16]

    // Default memberwise initializers are never public by default, so we
    // declare one manually.
    public init(
        /**
         * Empty when the camera did not name the mode; the points are still drawn.
         */areaMode: String, 
        /**
         * The AF image the coordinates are relative to, so the overlay can letterbox correctly.
         */imageWidth: UInt32, imageHeight: UInt32, points: [FfiAfPoint], 
        /**
         * Indices the camera reports as in focus, in the same units exiftool prints.
         */pointsInFocus: [UInt16]) {
        self.areaMode = areaMode
        self.imageWidth = imageWidth
        self.imageHeight = imageHeight
        self.points = points
        self.pointsInFocus = pointsInFocus
    }

    

    
}

#if compiler(>=6)
extension FfiAfInfo: Sendable {}
#endif

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public struct FfiConverterTypeFfiAfInfo: FfiConverterRustBuffer {
    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> FfiAfInfo {
        return
            try FfiAfInfo(
                areaMode: FfiConverterString.read(from: &buf), 
                imageWidth: FfiConverterUInt32.read(from: &buf), 
                imageHeight: FfiConverterUInt32.read(from: &buf), 
                points: FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiAfPoint.read(from: &buf), 
                pointsInFocus: FfiConverterSequenceUInt16.read(from: &buf)
        )
    }

    public static func write(_ value: FfiAfInfo, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        FfiConverterString.write(value.areaMode, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterUInt32.write(value.imageWidth, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterUInt32.write(value.imageHeight, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiAfPoint.write(value.points, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterSequenceUInt16.write(value.pointsInFocus, into: &buf)
    }
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiAfInfo_lift(_ buf: RustBuffer) throws -> FfiAfInfo {
    return try FfiConverterTypeFfiAfInfo.lift(buf)
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiAfInfo_lower(_ value: FfiAfInfo) -> RustBuffer {
    return FfiConverterTypeFfiAfInfo.lower(value)
}

public struct FfiBatch: Equatable, Hashable {
    public var id: UInt64
    public var index: UInt32
    /**
     * In capture order.
     */

    /**
     * True until visual signatures have settled this batch's boundaries.

    // declare one manually.

        /**
         * In capture order.

        /**
         * True until visual signatures have settled this batch's boundaries.
         */provisional: Bool) {
        self.id = id
        self.index = index
        self.photoIds = photoIds
        self.provisional = provisional

/**
 * One rating change, with everything undo needs to put it back (todo.md §6.3).
 */
public struct FfiChange: Equatable, Hashable {
    /**
     * Monotonic across the session, so the app can order changes it has already seen.
     */
    public var id: UInt64
    public var photo: UInt64
    public var batch: UInt64
    /**
     * The batch the change was made in, so undo can navigate back across a batch boundary.
     */
    public var batchIndex: UInt32
    public var before: FfiRating
    public var after: FfiRating

    // Default memberwise initializers are never public by default, so we
    // declare one manually.
    public init(
        /**
         * Monotonic across the session, so the app can order changes it has already seen.
         */id: UInt64, photo: UInt64, batch: UInt64, 
        /**
         * The batch the change was made in, so undo can navigate back across a batch boundary.
         */batchIndex: UInt32, before: FfiRating, after: FfiRating) {
        self.id = id
        self.photo = photo
        self.batch = batch
        self.batchIndex = batchIndex
        self.before = before
        self.after = after
    }

    

    
}

#if compiler(>=6)
extension FfiChange: Sendable {}
#endif

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public struct FfiConverterTypeFfiChange: FfiConverterRustBuffer {
    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> FfiChange {
        return
            try FfiChange(
                id: FfiConverterUInt64.read(from: &buf), 
                photo: FfiConverterUInt64.read(from: &buf), 
                batch: FfiConverterUInt64.read(from: &buf), 
                batchIndex: FfiConverterUInt32.read(from: &buf), 
                before: FfiConverterTypeFfiRating.read(from: &buf), 
                after: FfiConverterTypeFfiRating.read(from: &buf)
        )
    }

    public static func write(_ value: FfiChange, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        FfiConverterUInt64.write(value.id, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterUInt64.write(value.photo, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterUInt64.write(value.batch, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterUInt32.write(value.batchIndex, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterTypeFfiRating.write(value.before, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterTypeFfiRating.write(value.after, into: &buf)
    }
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiChange_lift(_ buf: RustBuffer) throws -> FfiChange {
    return try FfiConverterTypeFfiChange.lift(buf)
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiChange_lower(_ value: FfiChange) -> RustBuffer {
    return FfiConverterTypeFfiChange.lower(value)
}

/**
 * The rating mode is deliberately not here: the session plans with its own, so the preview
 * cannot disagree with the filmstrip about what a keep is (REV-78).
 */
public struct FfiFinishOptions: Equatable, Hashable {
    public var unkept: FfiUnkeptAction
    public var kept: FfiKeptAction

    // Default memberwise initializers are never public by default, so we
    // declare one manually.
    public init(unkept: FfiUnkeptAction, kept: FfiKeptAction) {
        self.unkept = unkept
        self.kept = kept
    }

    

    
}

#if compiler(>=6)
extension FfiFinishOptions: Sendable {}
#endif

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public struct FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishOptions: FfiConverterRustBuffer {
    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> FfiFinishOptions {
        return
            try FfiFinishOptions(
                unkept: FfiConverterTypeFfiUnkeptAction.read(from: &buf), 
                kept: FfiConverterTypeFfiKeptAction.read(from: &buf)
        )
    }

    public static func write(_ value: FfiFinishOptions, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        FfiConverterTypeFfiUnkeptAction.write(value.unkept, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterTypeFfiKeptAction.write(value.kept, into: &buf)
    }
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif

/**
 * What an execution, or an undo, did. Never silent: every failure is listed with its reason.
 */
public struct FfiFinishReport: Equatable, Hashable {
    public var done: UInt32
    public var failed: [FfiFileOpFailure]
    /**
     * False once a permanent delete has run.
     */
    public var undoable: Bool
    /**
     * Set by an undo when there was no Finish run to reverse.
     */
    public var nothingToUndo: Bool

    // Default memberwise initializers are never public by default, so we
    // declare one manually.
    public init(done: UInt32, failed: [FfiFileOpFailure], 
        /**
         * False once a permanent delete has run.
         */undoable: Bool, 
        /**
         * Set by an undo when there was no Finish run to reverse.
         */nothingToUndo: Bool) {
        self.done = done
        self.failed = failed
        self.undoable = undoable
        self.nothingToUndo = nothingToUndo
    }

    

    
}

#if compiler(>=6)
extension FfiFinishReport: Sendable {}
#endif

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public struct FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishReport: FfiConverterRustBuffer {
    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> FfiFinishReport {
        return
            try FfiFinishReport(
                done: FfiConverterUInt32.read(from: &buf), 
                failed: FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiFileOpFailure.read(from: &buf), 
                undoable: FfiConverterBool.read(from: &buf), 
                nothingToUndo: FfiConverterBool.read(from: &buf)
        )
    }

    public static func write(_ value: FfiFinishReport, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        FfiConverterUInt32.write(value.done, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiFileOpFailure.write(value.failed, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterBool.write(value.undoable, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterBool.write(value.nothingToUndo, into: &buf)
    }
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishReport_lift(_ buf: RustBuffer) throws -> FfiFinishReport {
    return try FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishReport.lift(buf)
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishReport_lower(_ value: FfiFinishReport) -> RustBuffer {
    return FfiConverterTypeFfiFinishReport.lower(value)
}


public struct FfiPhotoMeta: Equatable, Hashable {
    public var id: UInt64
    public var relPath: String
    public var companions: [String]
    public var kind: FfiFileKind
    public var fileSize: UInt64
    public var captureTime: FfiCaptureTime?
    public var shutterCount: UInt64?
    public var fileNumber: UInt32?
    public var cameraMake: String?
    public var cameraModel: String?
    public var cameraSerial: String?
    public var lensModel: String?
    public var focalLengthMm: Float?
    public var exposureTimeS: Float?
    public var fNumber: Float?
    public var iso: UInt32?
    public var exposureCompEv: Float?
    public var meteringMode: String?
    public var driveMode: String?
    public var shutterMode: String?
    public var orientation: UInt8
    public var width: UInt32
    public var height: UInt32
    public var af: FfiAfInfo?
    /**
     * The 1620x1080 `PRVW` JPEG. Not the display image — see `FfiPhotoMeta::full_preview`.
     */
    public var preview: FfiEmbeddedPreview?
    /**
     * The full-resolution JPEG, for display decodes straight from its bytes.
     */
    public var fullPreview: FfiEmbeddedPreview?
    public var warnings: [String]

    // Default memberwise initializers are never public by default, so we
    // declare one manually.
    public init(id: UInt64, relPath: String, companions: [String], kind: FfiFileKind, fileSize: UInt64, captureTime: FfiCaptureTime?, shutterCount: UInt64?, fileNumber: UInt32?, cameraMake: String?, cameraModel: String?, cameraSerial: String?, lensModel: String?, focalLengthMm: Float?, exposureTimeS: Float?, fNumber: Float?, iso: UInt32?, exposureCompEv: Float?, meteringMode: String?, driveMode: String?, shutterMode: String?, orientation: UInt8, width: UInt32, height: UInt32, af: FfiAfInfo?, 
        /**
         * The 1620x1080 `PRVW` JPEG. Not the display image — see `FfiPhotoMeta::full_preview`.
         */preview: FfiEmbeddedPreview?, 
        /**
         * The full-resolution JPEG, for display decodes straight from its bytes.
         */fullPreview: FfiEmbeddedPreview?, warnings: [String]) {
        self.id = id
        self.relPath = relPath
        self.companions = companions
        self.kind = kind
        self.fileSize = fileSize
        self.captureTime = captureTime
        self.shutterCount = shutterCount
        self.fileNumber = fileNumber
        self.cameraMake = cameraMake
        self.cameraModel = cameraModel
        self.cameraSerial = cameraSerial
        self.lensModel = lensModel
        self.focalLengthMm = focalLengthMm
        self.exposureTimeS = exposureTimeS
        self.fNumber = fNumber
        self.iso = iso
        self.exposureCompEv = exposureCompEv
        self.meteringMode = meteringMode
        self.driveMode = driveMode
        self.shutterMode = shutterMode
        self.orientation = orientation
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.af = af
        self.preview = preview
        self.fullPreview = fullPreview
        self.warnings = warnings
    }

    

    
}

extension FfiPhotoMeta: Sendable {}
#endif

@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif

    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> FfiPhotoMeta {
        return
            try FfiPhotoMeta(
                id: FfiConverterUInt64.read(from: &buf), 
                relPath: FfiConverterString.read(from: &buf), 
                companions: FfiConverterSequenceString.read(from: &buf), 
                kind: FfiConverterTypeFfiFileKind.read(from: &buf), 
                fileSize: FfiConverterUInt64.read(from: &buf), 
                captureTime: FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiCaptureTime.read(from: &buf), 
                shutterCount: FfiConverterOptionUInt64.read(from: &buf), 
                fileNumber: FfiConverterOptionUInt32.read(from: &buf), 
                cameraMake: FfiConverterOptionString.read(from: &buf), 
                cameraModel: FfiConverterOptionString.read(from: &buf), 
                cameraSerial: FfiConverterOptionString.read(from: &buf), 
                lensModel: FfiConverterOptionString.read(from: &buf), 
                focalLengthMm: FfiConverterOptionFloat.read(from: &buf), 
                exposureTimeS: FfiConverterOptionFloat.read(from: &buf), 
                fNumber: FfiConverterOptionFloat.read(from: &buf), 
                iso: FfiConverterOptionUInt32.read(from: &buf), 
                exposureCompEv: FfiConverterOptionFloat.read(from: &buf), 
                meteringMode: FfiConverterOptionString.read(from: &buf), 
                driveMode: FfiConverterOptionString.read(from: &buf), 
                shutterMode: FfiConverterOptionString.read(from: &buf), 
                orientation: FfiConverterUInt8.read(from: &buf), 
                width: FfiConverterUInt32.read(from: &buf), 
                height: FfiConverterUInt32.read(from: &buf), 
                af: FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiAfInfo.read(from: &buf), 
                preview: FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiEmbeddedPreview.read(from: &buf), 
                fullPreview: FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiEmbeddedPreview.read(from: &buf), 
                warnings: FfiConverterSequenceString.read(from: &buf)
        )
    }

    public static func write(_ value: FfiPhotoMeta, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        FfiConverterUInt64.write(value.id, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterString.write(value.relPath, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterSequenceString.write(value.companions, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterTypeFfiFileKind.write(value.kind, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterUInt64.write(value.fileSize, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiCaptureTime.write(value.captureTime, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionUInt64.write(value.shutterCount, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionUInt32.write(value.fileNumber, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionString.write(value.cameraMake, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionString.write(value.cameraModel, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionString.write(value.cameraSerial, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionString.write(value.lensModel, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionFloat.write(value.focalLengthMm, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionFloat.write(value.exposureTimeS, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionFloat.write(value.fNumber, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionUInt32.write(value.iso, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionFloat.write(value.exposureCompEv, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionString.write(value.meteringMode, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionString.write(value.driveMode, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionString.write(value.shutterMode, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterUInt8.write(value.orientation, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterUInt32.write(value.width, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterUInt32.write(value.height, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiAfInfo.write(value.af, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiEmbeddedPreview.write(value.preview, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiEmbeddedPreview.write(value.fullPreview, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterSequenceString.write(value.warnings, into: &buf)
    }
}

public struct FfiRating: Equatable, Hashable {
    /**
     * 0..=5 in stars mode. Out-of-range is clamped by the core, never rejected, so a slider
     * that overshoots cannot throw at the user.
     */
    public var stars: UInt8
    public var flag: FfiFlag
    public var label: FfiColorLabel?
    /**
     * Keep / Not keep mode.
     */
    public var keep: Bool

    // Default memberwise initializers are never public by default, so we
    // declare one manually.
    public init(
        /**
         * 0..=5 in stars mode. Out-of-range is clamped by the core, never rejected, so a slider
         * that overshoots cannot throw at the user.
         */stars: UInt8, flag: FfiFlag, label: FfiColorLabel?, 
        /**
         * Keep / Not keep mode.
         */keep: Bool) {
        self.stars = stars
        self.flag = flag
        self.label = label
        self.keep = keep
    }

    

    
}

#if compiler(>=6)
extension FfiRating: Sendable {}
#endif

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public struct FfiConverterTypeFfiRating: FfiConverterRustBuffer {
    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> FfiRating {
        return
            try FfiRating(
                stars: FfiConverterUInt8.read(from: &buf), 
                flag: FfiConverterTypeFfiFlag.read(from: &buf), 
                label: FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiColorLabel.read(from: &buf), 
                keep: FfiConverterBool.read(from: &buf)
        )
    }

    public static func write(_ value: FfiRating, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        FfiConverterUInt8.write(value.stars, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterTypeFfiFlag.write(value.flag, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterOptionTypeFfiColorLabel.write(value.label, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterBool.write(value.keep, into: &buf)
    }
}


#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiRating_lift(_ buf: RustBuffer) throws -> FfiRating {
    return try FfiConverterTypeFfiRating.lift(buf)
}

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public func FfiConverterTypeFfiRating_lower(_ value: FfiRating) -> RustBuffer {
    return FfiConverterTypeFfiRating.lower(value)
}


public struct FfiScanResult: Equatable, Hashable {
    /**
     * In `rel_path` order. Ordering into batches is core-batch's job, not the scanner's.
     */
    public var photos: [FfiPhotoMeta]
    /**
     * Files found and not understood, each with the reason. Never empty because a parse failed
     * quietly (todo.md §8).
     */
    public var skipped: [FfiSkipped]

    // Default memberwise initializers are never public by default, so we
    // declare one manually.
    public init(
        /**
         * In `rel_path` order. Ordering into batches is core-batch's job, not the scanner's.
         */photos: [FfiPhotoMeta], 
        /**
         * Files found and not understood, each with the reason. Never empty because a parse failed
         * quietly (todo.md §8).
         */skipped: [FfiSkipped]) {
        self.photos = photos
        self.skipped = skipped
    }

    

    
}

#if compiler(>=6)
extension FfiScanResult: Sendable {}
#endif

#if swift(>=5.8)
@_documentation(visibility: private)
#endif
public struct FfiConverterTypeFfiScanResult: FfiConverterRustBuffer {
    public static func read(from buf: inout (data: Data, offset: Data.Index)) throws -> FfiScanResult {
        return
            try FfiScanResult(
                photos: FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiPhotoMeta.read(from: &buf), 
                skipped: FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiSkipped.read(from: &buf)
        )
    }

    public static func write(_ value: FfiScanResult, into buf: inout [UInt8]) {
        FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiPhotoMeta.write(value.photos, into: &buf)
        FfiConverterSequenceTypeFfiSkipped.write(value.skipped, into: &buf)
    }
}
